column1: # Human corrections for B1 Quasqueton LOWER level (level 2).
# SEPARATE FILE ON PURPOSE. build.apply_corrections(db, file, level) stamps
# EVERY row at the level it is passed -- there is no level column -- so sharing
# b1_corrections.tsv between the two sheets would silently write level 1's
# coordinates onto level 2. Keep them apart.
#   what   = cell | edge | feature | member | room
#   orient = V (east side of x,y) | H (north side of x,y) | - for cells
# Applied THREE times by the rebuild: after build, after markers.py --apply,
# 1. FALSE WALLS: the middle-half window misses an oblique cave opening
# extract._edge samples the middle HALF of a boundary (trim=0.25) and takes the
# MEDIAN of that window. On the upper level, where a doorway is cut in the
# middle of a straight wall, that is right. On a CAVERN sheet it is not: the
# floor crosses a grid line wherever the cave happens to run, and very often
# that is within a couple of feet of the cell CORNER. The window then sees
# nothing but rock, `gap` is 0, and the boundary falls through to `wall`.
# Measured instead over the FULL boundary length: perpendicular rock thickness
# at every pixel, and the longest RUN of positions thinner than 4.5 px (the
# printed-ruling band). That run is, in feet, how wide the opening actually is.
#   wall edges between two walkable squares      268
#     clear run 0-2 px   (rock spans it)         100   left alone
#     clear run >= 8 px  (>= 2 ft of open floor) 125   OPENED, below
# Validated by eye: all 125 were rendered as crops of the printed page with the
# boundary drawn on (scratchpad lv2/runs8_0..2.png) and in every one the white
# cave floor visibly crosses the line. A stratified control sample of 18 more
# at run 0-7 (lv2/val_runs.png) showed rock spanning the boundary in each.
# Three sub-causes are worth naming, because they are the same class of error
# the upper level's audit found and they will recur:
#   * an AREA LABEL straddling a cell boundary. label_boxes shields a cell's
#     INTERIOR (inset 0.15) but not its border, so the half of a straddling
#     numeral that sits near the boundary joins the rock mass and fabricates a
#     wall between the two squares of its own room: (4,37,V) under "55",
#   * a drawn SYMBOL doing the same: the statue at (3,18,H), the covered pit

#   edges   wall 2069  open 1378  door 4  secret 4  stairs 1
#   walkable 923   reached 925*   UNREACHED 0     from the level-1 stairs (20,13)
#   * `reached` exceeds `walkable` by 2 because dmap.reachable's corner step for
#     passage='diagonal' does not re-check that the destination is walkable, so
#     it counts two squares this file has set to `solid`. Pre-existing in
#     dmap.py, harmless here, worth knowing before the number is compared.
# THE SECRET-DOOR SEAL TEST. Seal each secret edge in a COPY and re-flood:
#   (30,6,H)   area 40 -> 13 squares cut off, area 40 among them.  LOAD-BEARING
# That is a finding about the MAP, not about the extraction. Only area 40 is
# actually sealed behind its secret door on the printed sheet. The hidden
# corridor 55 - 54 - 53 is a SHORTCUT: the caverns loop, and areas 54, 55 and
# 56 are all reachable the long way round, through the covered-pit junction at
# (7,23)-(8,22). Do not tell a player that the treasure cave can only be found
# through a secret door; the map does not say so.
# ROOM EXTENTS ARE THE WEAK PART OF THIS LEVEL AND SHOULD NOT BE QUOTED.
# extents.py splits room from corridor on "a room contains a 2x2 block of open
# floor and a corridor does not", and grows areas from their labels by nearest-
# seed BFS. On a stronghold that is right. On a cavern nothing is rectilinear,
# every wide bulge in a winding passage passes the 2x2 test, and the growth
# runs until it meets another label. The result: area 51 gets 96 squares and
# area 53 gets 180, while 44 gets 2 and 50 gets 4. 175 squares come out "wide
# but unlabelled". The module gives no room dimension anywhere on this level,
# so there is nothing to cross-check against either. Treat `cells.room` here as
# "nearest numbered area", not as "this square is inside room N".
# DAY 140: a false `feature='outside'` at (2,9) produced an invented plot
# beat. `outside_cells()` sweeps the outer frame ring (here, columns/rows
# within 2 of the sheet's edge) and tags anything in it that isn't cleanly
# 'open' terrain as page-border scenery, on the assumption B1's one real
# entrance is the only non-scenery square in that ring. (2,9) is 'mixed'
# terrain, two columns from the left edge, and got swept up by that rule --
# but the DM read it as "feature: outside" mid-session and narrated a second
# cave mouth, daylight, a draft, from a DATA-PIPELINE HOUSEKEEPING TAG that
# has nothing to do with the fiction. Checked against the actual page render
# (dpi/page/channel from the levels table): columns 0-1 at this row are
# genuinely blank rock/margin, but column 2 is part of the SAME connected
# winding passage running north-south through x=2, y=6-12 -- real cave
# floor, not scenery, not a second entrance. 51 other 'mixed' cells carry
# this same tag across level 2 and have not been individually checked;
# treat any of them the same way before narrating from one.
